articles.title: Inside Health - How well will new endometriosis tests work? - BBC Sounds
articles.summary: And the barriers queer couples can face in accessing fertility treatment.
articles.body: Women with endometriosis often spend years searching for answers. On average, it can take around a decade to get a diagnosis. So could a new generation of tests, which are far less invasive than what's available today, help cut that wait from years to days? Inside Health is looking at what those tests involve and how well they might work in the real world. We'll also hear from one couple about their difficult journey to starting a family - and explore why many queer couples still face huge hurdles when trying to access fertility treatment here in the UK. And as the clocks go back, Laura looks at why a change of just one hour can result in 'social jet lag' or 'first class sleep'. Why are the first few days the hardest - and what we can do to make 'falling back' into autumn and 'springing forward' in March easier on our bodies? Presenter: Laura Foster Producer: Gerry Holt Editor: Ilan Goodman Production coordinator: Stu Laws Sound engineer: Sue Maillot The show was made by the BBC’s Audio Science Unit in collaboration with The Open University.

articles.title: Newcastle AmberSide show opens with call to young photographers
articles.summary: AmberSide hopes to strengthen and expand its Newcastle archive with its latest exhibition.
articles.body:
A new exhibition exploring how a city has changed over time has coincided with an open call for young photographers.

Under Development: What Happens When Cities Change? has opened at Newcastle Contemporary Art gallery, featuring images which span more than 50 years from the AmberSide Collection.

Running alongside the exhibition, submissions have opened for Newcastle Now, which has asked photographers under 25 to capture their changing surroundings.

Creative director of AmberSide, Ellen Stone, said she hoped the archive would be a "stronger resource" following the exhibition.

The exhibition also features photographs from Four Corners Archive based in Tower Hamlets in London.

AmberSide said as both areas grew through river trade and industry, both saw large areas of working-class housing cleared and rebuilt and were hit hard by the loss of industries that had shaped them.

Stone said the exhibition was particularly important today, as both areas were once again going through a period of regeneration.

Sirkka-Liisa Konttinen is one of the photographers featured in the exhibition.

The Finnish photographer moved to Byker in 1969 and started capturing every day life in Newcastle's inner city as it was undergoing great change with the post-war terraced housing being torn down.

She returned again in 2003 to take photos in the Byker Wall Estate, which had replaced the old housing.

Stone said the photos in the archive helped people understand how the city looked and felt in the past, but now they needed to look to the future.

"We have this incredible wealth of resource from our collection, but we're looking for images from young people today about the city," she said.

"Hopefully we'll leave the exhibition with an even stronger resource than we started with."

The exhibition will run until 29 November, meanwhile submissions for the Newcastle Now open call is open until midnight on 1 December.

articles.title: Casos de Ebola passam de 10 mil no Congo  | G1
articles.standfirst: Surto atinge oito províncias e enfrenta desinformação e ataques contra profissionais de saúde.
articles.summary: Surto atinge oito províncias e enfrenta desinformação e ataques contra profissionais de saúde.
articles.body:
Pacientes são testados para Ebola no Congo, — Foto: Diuedonne Dirole/AFP

O surto de Ebola, que avança rapidamente no Congo, chegou a 10 mil casos confirmados, mostraram dados do governo nesta terça-feira, enquanto autoridades de saúde correm para conter a disseminação da doença em vários países africanos.

É o surto de Ebola de crescimento mais rápido da história, e quase metade das 10.060 pessoas com diagnóstico confirmado morreu, segundo dados do Ministério da Saúde do Congo. Isso também faz dele o surto mais mortal da doença na história do país.

O surto, declarado em maio, é causado pelo raro vírus Bundibugyo, para o qual não há vacina nem tratamento aprovados. As equipes de resposta enfrentam conflitos armados, estradas em más condições e violência de moradores, alimentada pela desconfiança e pela desinformação. Esses obstáculos aumentam a dificuldade de convencer as pessoas a relatar sintomas e aceitar atendimento em comunidades que enfrentam há anos episódios de violência e sucessivas epidemias.

Em comparação com o surto de Ebola na África Ocidental entre 2014 e 2016, o maior e mais mortal da história, com mais de 28 mil casos e mais de 11 mil mortes, o atual surto registrou, desde que foi declarado, pelo menos três vezes mais casos e mortes no mesmo intervalo de tempo.

Um profissional de saúde queniano verifica a temperatura de viajantes que cruzam a fronteira de Uganda para o Quênia. — Foto: Andrew Kasuku/AP

A doença se espalhou pela África mais do que qualquer surto anterior de Ebola, alcançando três regiões, com casos registrados também no Quênia e na Nigéria. Até agora, houve registros em cinco países, incluindo Uganda e França, que atualmente não têm casos ativos.

Um problema recorrente na disseminação da doença na África é o que parece ser uma vigilância deficiente, já que a maioria dos primeiros casos foi confirmada muito depois de as pessoas começarem a apresentar sintomas ou após terem viajado.

80% dos novos casos estão fora dos contatos monitorados

No Congo, a doença se espalhou para 66 zonas de saúde em oito províncias, ante três zonas quando o surto foi declarado, em maio. Profissionais envolvidos na resposta disseram à Associated Press que centros de tratamento em algumas dessas áreas estão sobrecarregados, que parte da população continua desconfiada e reage com violência e que profissionais de saúde têm feito greves regularmente contra atrasos ou falta de pagamento dos salários.

“Algumas pessoas ainda parecem não entender a gravidade da situação, embora estejam diretamente expostas ao risco”, disse Sephora Bgosi, integrante da equipe responsável por sepultamentos de vítimas de Ebola na província de Ituri, epicentro do surto. “O Ebola é extremamente perigoso e pode ser mortal”, afirmou Bgosi.

Cerca de 80% dos casos registrados ainda são identificados fora do grupo de contatos monitorados, o que indica a existência de cadeias de transmissão desconhecidas pelas autoridades de saúde. Segundo o Centro Africano de Controle e Prevenção de Doenças (CDC África), pelo menos 95% dos casos registrados deveriam estar entre contatos conhecidos para que as autoridades pudessem considerar o surto amplamente sob controle.

Profissional de saúde com roupas de proteção é desinfetado por um colega dentro de um centro de tratamento para pacientes com Ebola em Beni, na província de Kivu do Norte, no leste do Congo — Foto: Sebastien Kitsa Musayi/AP

Ao menos metade das mortes registradas ocorreu entre pessoas que não chegaram a ser internadas em centros de tratamento, um sinal de que, em muitas regiões, moradores ainda não estão relatando sintomas.

Em várias áreas, profissionais de saúde enfrentam desde dificuldades básicas, como falta de veículos adequados, até situações mais complexas, como convencer famílias a entregar parentes doentes ou que morreram da doença para que sejam sepultados de forma segura.

Na semana passada, na zona de saúde de Nia Nia, na província de Ituri, alguns profissionais envolvidos na resposta ao Ebola, incluindo agentes de vigilância e de mobilização comunitária, entraram em greve por causa de bônus não pagos desde o fim de agosto, problema recorrente em diversas localidades atingidas.

Mais de cinco meses após a declaração do surto, profissionais de saúde continuam sendo atacados por moradores. No sábado, um enfermeiro foi morto e outro profissional ficou gravemente ferido enquanto atendiam a um alerta de Ebola em Bafwasende, na província de Tshopo.

O surto prejudicou serviços essenciais de saúde, que já sofriam com falta de recursos e sobrecarga, e desviou a atenção de outros surtos enfrentados pelo país, como o de cólera.

Mais mulheres grávidas estão morrendo porque evitam hospitais por medo de infecção e isolamento. Com isso, a mortalidade materna dobrou em algumas províncias pouco depois da declaração do surto.

A epidemia também afetou serviços rotineiros de saúde, como a vacinação infantil, interrompeu as aulas de crianças em regiões onde milhões já estão fora da escola, provocou trauma e estigma entre famílias atingidas e agravou as dificuldades de subsistência de muitas pessoas que já enfrentavam condições precárias.

articles.title: Lula cresce 3 vezes mais que Flávio Bolsonaro em Uberaba no 2º turno | G1
articles.standfirst: Comparação dos resultados mostra que o petista foi o candidato que mais ganhou apoio entre os turnos e ampliou desempenho em diversas regiões de Uberaba.
articles.summary: Lula em Uberaba avançou 27% entre os turnos e superou o ritmo de crescimento de Flávio Bolsonaro, conquistando novos apoios em diversas regiões da cidade.
articles.body:
Lula discursa na avenida Paulista — Foto: REUTERS

Lula (PT) foi o candidato que mais avançou entre o primeiro e o segundo turno das Eleições 2026 em Uberaba . Embora Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) tenha mantido a liderança geral no município e na maior parte dos bairros da cidade, o crescimento do petista foi mais de três vezes superior ao registrado pelo adversário na etapa final da disputa presidencial.

Com 68.891 votos na cidade no primeiro turno e 87.606 no segundo, Lula cresceu 27,16% entre os dois dias de votação. Já Flávio Bolsonaro passou de 91.107 para 98.581 entre os turnos, um aumento de 8,2% . Nessa perspectiva, o petista ampliou os votos em Uberaba em 3,3 vezes mais que o bolsonarista .

A comparação dos resultados mostra que Lula conseguiu ampliar a votação em todos os bairros onde já era competitivo e ainda atraiu parte do eleitorado que havia optado por outros candidatos ou mesmo pelo voto branco e nulo e pela abstenção no primeiro turno. O movimento permitiu ao petista reduzir a diferença em diversos pontos da cidade e fortalecer a presença eleitoral em Uberaba .

Confira no gráfico abaixo o desempenho dos dois candidatos nos dois turnos em Uberaba.

Flávio manteve liderança do 1º turno, mas Lula teve maior avanço

O segundo turno consolidou um cenário de dois movimentos distintos. De um lado, Flávio Bolsonaro preservou os principais redutos e continuou liderando na maior parte dos bairros com local de votação. De outro, Lula apresentou crescimento proporcional mais intenso, ampliando a participação no eleitorado de forma generalizada, e virando votos em sete bairros .

Na prática, isso significa que, embora o mapa eleitoral da cidade ainda tenha permanecido majoritariamente favorável a Flávio Bolsonaro, a velocidade de crescimento do petista foi significativamente maior entre uma etapa e outra da eleição.

Apesar do avanço lulista e da conquista da liderança em sete bairros, o segundo turno não alterou completamente o equilíbrio político da cidade .

Flávio Bolsonaro continuou dominante em bairros que concentram algumas das maiores votações proporcionais da cidade, especialmente em regiões centrais, mantendo uma base eleitoral sólida .

Ao mesmo tempo, Lula fortaleceu o desempenho em áreas populosas e ampliou a presença em bairros onde a disputa era mais equilibrada .

O resultado final revela uma Uberaba politicamente dividida , mas marcada por um movimento claro de crescimento mais acelerado do eleitorado lulista entre os dois turnos.

articles.title: Unifesp suspende aulas após morte de engenheiro agredido em Santos | G1
articles.standfirst: Marcelo de Oliveira Rocha, de 30 anos, foi agredido e roubado após sair de um evento político para ir ao banheiro, em Santos (SP). A Unifesp e o grupo Esquerdantina cobram a apuração rigorosa dos fatos.
articles.summary: Marcelo de Oliveira Rocha, de 30 anos, foi agredido e roubado após sair de um evento político para ir ao banheiro, em Santos (SP).
articles.body:
A Universidade Federal de São Paulo (Unifesp) suspendeu as aulas e atividades desta terça-feira (27) no Campus Baixada Santista, no litoral de São Paulo, em luto pela morte do engenheiro Marcelo de Oliveira Rocha . Ele foi espancado após participar de um ato pró-Lula. Em nota, a instituição informou que a decisão foi tomada em "sinal de respeito e solidariedade à família, aos amigos e a toda a comunidade acadêmica".

Marcelo era mestrando em Ecologia Marinha, na Unifesp. Ele participou de uma apresentação da Banda Esquerdantina , em apoio à reeleição do presidente Lula (PT) na madrugada deste sábado (24). Ele se afastou do evento para ir ao banheiro, quando foi abordado e agredido por ao menos sete homens, que fizeram uma live durante o crime (veja acima) .

O estudante teve a morte cerebral confirmada pela família no domingo (25 ), quando foi transferido da Santa Casa de Santos para o Hospital São Paulo, da Unifesp. Segundo o pai dele, Marcelo Rodrigues da Rocha, faltava um exame para confirmar a irreversibilidade do quadro, cujo resultado saiu por volta das 17h desta segunda-feira (26).

Unifesp suspende aulas em luto pela morte do estudante Marcelo de Oliveira Rocha — Foto: Redes sociais e Reprodução

Formado em Engenharia Ambiental pela Unifesp, Marcelo era mestrando em Ecologia Marinha na instituição. Conforme apurado pelo g1 , ele era muito ativo nos projetos da universidade, participando de atividades esportivas e da bateria universitária da instituição.

Em nota, assinada pela direção do Campus Baixada Santista e pelos Institutos do Mar (IMar) e Saúde e Sociedade (ISS), a Unifesp informou sobre a morte do aluno e suspendeu as aulas e demais atividades acadêmicas do Campus nesta terça-feira (27).

"As direções reafirmam sua solidariedade aos familiares e amigos de Marcelo neste momento de dor e seguem acompanhando a situação em conjunto com a Direção do Campus, a Pró-Reitoria de Assuntos Estudantis e Políticas Afirmativas (Praepa) e a Reitoria da Unifesp", disse o comunicado.

Anteriormente, a universidade havia emitido uma nota de repúdio à violência sofrida pelo estudante e, após a morte, divulgou uma nota de pesar.

"A gravidade do ocorrido exige a apuração rigorosa das circunstâncias e motivações da agressão, bem como a identificação e responsabilização dos envolvidos”, dizia a nota, divulgada nas redes sociais.

Marcelo de Oliveira Rocha foi agredido após se afastar de um ato político pró-Lula em Santos — Foto: Redes sociais

A Bateria Repicapau e a Torcida Organizada Baixada de Gaza, ambas da Unifesp, lamentaram a morte do jovem, também nas redes sociais.

A bateria Repicapau prestou solidariedade aos familiares, amigos e colegas de Marcelo, que atuou como ritmista e era muito querido. "Você sempre nos trouxe muita alegria, paixão, boas risadas, companheirismo e muito samba. Cada tacaticata tocado será para e por você! Não deixaremos que tamanha crueldade passe impune", publicou.

Grupo fez live agredindo e roubando engenheiro que se afastou de ato pró-Lula em Santos, SP — Foto: Reprodução

Já a torcida organizada da Unifesp relembrou os momentos em que Marcelo jogou pela instituição, descrevendo-o como "atleta que tantas vezes apoiamos nas arquibancadas e que faz parte da nossa história e comunidade".

"Nossa torcida se une em luto, solidariedade e saudade diante de uma violência que jamais deveria ter acontecido", escreveu o grupo, dizendo que ficam a saudade, a indignação e a luta por justiça. "Sua história não será esquecida".

Marcelo de Oliveira Rocha, de 30 anos, foi abordado por ao menos sete homens em Santos, SP — Foto: Reprodução/Instagram

A Secretaria de Segurança Pública de São Paulo (SSP-SP) informou que o caso é investigado pelo 4º Distrito Policial (DP) de Santos.

"Equipes da unidade analisam as imagens divulgadas e trabalham em busca de câmeras de monitoramento e outros elementos que auxiliem na identificação e prisão dos autores, bem como no esclarecimento dos fatos", afirmou a SSP-SP.

A SSP-SP disse que, segundo o boletim de ocorrência, "a vítima foi agredida por diversos indivíduos e teve o celular e outros pertences roubados".

Segundo testemunhas ouvidas pelo g1 , os amigos estranharam a demora de Marcelo no banheiro e começaram a procurá-lo. Ainda de acordo com os relatos, o engenheiro foi encontrado desacordado na esquina da Avenida Conselheiro Nébias com a Rua Henrique Ablas.

A Prefeitura de Santos informou que o Serviço de Atendimento Móvel de Urgência (Samu) foi acionado e encaminhou Marcelo à Santa Casa de Santos, onde ele ficou internado. A Polícia Militar também foi acionada, mas a vítima já havia sido socorrida quando os agentes chegaram ao local.

Marcelo de Oliveira Rocha, de 30 anos, foi espancado após se afastar de um ato político em Santos, SP — Foto: Reprodução/Instagram

Por meio de nota, a Esquerdantina confirmou ao g1 que Marcelo foi agredido e deixado inconsciente no local, onde foi socorrido. O grupo afirmou que exige "a rápida apuração e consequente punição aos responsáveis".

Embora a motivação da agressão ainda não tenha sido esclarecida, a Esquerdantina também manifestou repúdio à homofobia.

"Manifestamos nossa solidariedade à vítima e seus familiares, bem como nosso firme repúdio à homofobia, alertando para os riscos que todos corremos ao naturalizar, proteger ou promover o ódio como método de intimidação política", ressaltou.

articles.title: Homem é flagrado furtando produtos em supermercado de Búzios | G1
articles.standfirst: Câmeras de segurança registraram o suspeito escondendo iogurte, azeite e geleia na roupa e na mochila; mercadorias furtadas foram avaliadas em cerca de R$ 120.
articles.summary: Câmeras de segurança registraram o suspeito escondendo iogurte, azeite e geleia na roupa e na mochila; mercadorias furtadas foram avaliadas em cerca de R$ 120.
articles.body:
Um homem foi flagrado por câmeras de segurança furtando itens como geleia, iogurte e azeite de um supermercado na Avenida José Bento Ribeiro Dantas, em Manguinhos, em Armação dos Búzios , na Região dos Lagos do Rio, neste domingo (25). Os produtos foram avaliados em aproximadamente R$120.

Segundo o relato do supermercado, a ação ocorreu por volta das 13h10. Segundo as imagens, o homem entrou no estabelecimento aparentando ser um cliente e seguiu até o setor de laticínios, onde pegou um iogurte e o colocou no bolso.

Em seguida, circulou pelos corredores até chegar ao setor de cereais, óleos e azeites. Ele permaneceu alguns instantes no local, retirou uma unidade de azeite da gôndola e a guardou na mochila. Depois, foi a outro corredor, onde também furtou uma unidade de geleia.

Um boletim de ocorrência foi registrado na delegacia. As imagens das câmeras de segurança estão disponíveis para apresentação às autoridades policiais.

Câmeras de segurança flagraram o furto das mercadorias. — Foto: Divulgação

articles.title: Paulo Freire em Angicos vira patrimônio cultural imaterial do RN | G1
articles.standfirst: Lei sancionada pelo governo estadual reconhece legado da alfabetização de adultos realizada em 1963 e prevê preservação de memórias e práticas pedagógicas.
articles.summary: Lei sancionada no RN torna a experiência de Paulo Freire em Angicos patrimônio cultural imaterial para preservar o legado da alfabetização de adultos de 1963.
articles.body:
A experiência das “40 Horas de Angicos”, coordenada pelo educador Paulo Freire em 1963, na cidade de Angicos, foi reconhecida como Patrimônio Cultural Imaterial do Rio Grande do Norte. A medida foi publicada na edição do Diário Oficial desta terça-feira (27).

O projeto de alfabetização foi desenvolvido no município de Angicos, no interior do estado. O reconhecimento abrange as memórias, os relatos orais, os saberes e as práticas pedagógicas associados às pessoas e comunidades que participaram da experiência.

De acordo com a lei, o objetivo é preservar a memória coletiva dos participantes, incentivar pesquisas e divulgar referências históricas e culturais do projeto. A medida também busca transmitir esse legado às futuras gerações e valorizar a importância de Angicos para a história da educação brasileira.

O texto esclarece que o reconhecimento não substitui os procedimentos administrativos de registro e inventário previstos nas normas de proteção do patrimônio cultural. Também não obriga a rede estadual de ensino a adotar um método pedagógico específico nem altera os currículos escolares.

Em 1963, Freire levou uma experiência inédita de educação popular para a cidade de Angicos, no Oeste do Rio Grande do Norte, que à época tinha cerca de 9,5 mil habitantes. O educador tinha uma meta ousada: alfabetizar adultos em 40 horas. A primeira turma teve 380 participantes e cerca de 300 concluíram o curso, que começou em 28 de janeiro e terminou no dia 2 de abril.

O método Paulo Freire estimula a alfabetização dos adultos mediante a discussão de suas experiências de vida entre si, através de palavras presentes na realidade dos alunos, que são decodificadas para a aquisição da palavra escrita e da compreensão do mundo.

Monumento em homenagem a Paulo Freire em Angicos — Foto: Raiane Miranda

Paulo Freire desenvolveu um método de alfabetização baseado nas experiências de vida das pessoas. Em vez de buscar a alfabetização por meio de cartilhas e ensinar, por exemplo, “o boi baba” e “vovó viu a uva”, ele trabalhava as chamadas “palavras geradoras” a partir da realidade do cidadão.

Por exemplo, um trabalhador de fábrica podia aprender “tijolo”, “cimento”, enquanto um agricultor aprenderia palavras como “cana”, “enxada”, “terra” e “colheita”. A construção de novos vocábulos é baseada a partir da decodificação fonética dessas palavras.

A vinda de Paulo Freire ao Rio Grande do Norte começou a ser articulada em 1962 pelo então governador Aluízio Alves - que nasceu em Angicos - e foi intermediada pelo secretário de educação Calazans Fernandes.

A ideia era expandir o programa de Paulo Freire por todo estado para diminuir os índices de analfabetismo, mas o educador foi exilado em 1964 após o golpe militar sob a acusação de subversão.

articles.title: Qualidade do ar no Amazonas: Fumaça e 2,3 mil focos de incêndio | G1
articles.standfirst: Maior concentração de poluentes foi registrada em Itapiranga, onde o sensor do Sistema Eletrônico de Vigilância Ambiental (Selva), da UEA, indicava 112,5 microgramas por metro cúbico (µg/m³).
articles.summary: Qualidade do ar no Amazonas é afetada por 2,3 mil focos de incêndio; Itapiranga registra maior poluição com 112,5 µg/m³ segundo monitoramento da UEA.
articles.body:
Céu de Itacoatiara na Região Metropolitana de Manaus encoberto por fumaça nesta terça-feira (27) — Foto: Liam Cavalcante/Rede Amazônica

Municípios do Amazonas registraram qualidade do ar entre moderada e muito ruim na manhã desta terça-feira (27), segundo dados do Sistema Eletrônico de Vigilância Ambiental (Selva), da Universidade do Estado do Amazonas ( UEA ). No mesmo período, Manaus apresentava qualidade do ar moderada em todos os sensores da plataforma.

A situação ocorre em meio ao registro de incêndios florestais no estado. Dados do Painel do Fogo apontam 2.330 focos de incêndio no Amazonas no período de um mês.

A maior concentração de poluentes foi registrada em Itapiranga , onde o sensor do Selva indicava 112,5 microgramas por metro cúbico (µg/m³) . Em Itacoatiara , o índice era de 107,6 µg/m³, considerado ruim.

Outros municípios também apresentavam níveis elevados de partículas na atmosfera. Em Nhamundá , a concentração chegava a 80,2 µg/m³, enquanto, em Urucurituba , era de 77,1 µg/m³. Nos dois municípios, a qualidade do ar era classificada como muito ruim.

Em Parintins , o índice era de 63,2 µg/m³. Já em Barreirinha , chegava a 62,8 µg/m³. Nos dois municípios e em Boa Vista do Ramos , a qualidade do ar era considerada ruim.

Na segunda-feira (26), militares do Corpo de Bombeiros Militar do Amazonas (CBMAM) chegaram a Parintins para reforçar o combate aos incêndios florestais. Segundo a corporação, as equipes atuarão exclusivamente na zona rural do município.

Os bombeiros também receberam materiais e equipamentos para as operações. Entre eles está um kit pick-up, que permite adaptar uma caminhonete para combater incêndios em áreas de difícil acesso.

Queimadas no Pará podem levar fumaça ao Amazonas

Na segunda-feira (26), o governador do Amazonas, Roberto Cidade, afirmou que as queimadas no sul do Pará podem levar fumaça ao estado nos próximos dias . Segundo ele, os focos de incêndio estão concentrados principalmente na região de Itaituba, próxima à divisa entre os dois estados .

Durante uma coletiva de imprensa, Cidade disse que o governo do Amazonas pretende entrar em contato com o governo do Pará para discutir medidas de combate aos incêndios.

De acordo com o governador, a fumaça não deve chegar imediatamente, mas pode atingir o Amazonas em dois ou três dias.

"Grande parte de onde está tendo queimadas é no sul do Pará, é ali em Itaituba, na fronteira com o nosso estado, ali no Baixo Amazonas. Nós já estamos trabalhando para que a gente possa fazer a nossa parte aqui no nosso estado, mas também vou pedir junto com a nossa equipe para entrar em contato com o governo do Pará", afirmou.

Fumaça continua encobrindo céu de Parintins, no interior do Amazonas — Foto: Jean Beltrão/Rede Amazônica

articles.title: Emotional reunions as photographer recreates shots 46 years on
articles.summary: Sam Hill spent months tracking down the "special generation" he photographed as teenagers in 1980.
articles.body:
Back in 1980, photography student Sam Hill roamed the streets of Preston looking for young people who stood out - the mods, the punks, the free spirits.

He would stop them, take their picture, and move on.

"I think I caught a special generation," said Sam.

"A lot of free-spirited young people. I never asked their names.

"I just took the photograph, thought 'this looks great' and thanked them."

But over the next five decades, those faces never left him.

After retiring from his career, not in photography but graphic design, Sam set out on a remarkable mission.

Armed with nothing more than a collection of pictures, he spent months tracking down the strangers he had photographed as teenagers.

The search involved online appeals, social media trawls, emails, phone calls and countless conversations.

What followed was a series of emotional reunions and an Alternative Kids exhibition at Preston's Harris Museum.

Sam said the biggest surprise was not discovering what became of the teenagers in his photographs, but the emotions his endeavour brought up.

"It made me feel better about human beings," he said.

"I can honestly say I've left every meeting enriched and uplifted."

Among those he tracked down was Ray Balch, who spent time in care as a teenager and found belonging among Preston's punk and new wave scene.

"There was a close-knit community of punks," he said.

At the exhibition, Ray showed his photo to his wife and became emotional reflecting on the life that followed.

"I always wanted a relationship and love," he said.

"And I found that with my wife two years after the photos were taken."

He was photographed standing in front of William Routledge, who admitted he was "young and dumb" when Sam photographed him.

"I'd been doing well in school until punk came along," he said.

Over the years, he lost friends to drink and drugs, but he now runs a men's mental health group helping others through difficult times.

"I've probably saved a couple of people that might not have otherwise been here," William said.

Sam found that reuniting photos with the families of people who are no longer here was one of the most rewarding parts of the process.

Best friends Debbie Consiglio and Zena Gabrysch were individually photographed by Sam along with Zena's boyfriend, Alan Burton.

Two days later, they were on their way to an Adam and the Ants gig, when Zena died in a car accident.

Zena's brother Stefan Gybrisch, along with Debbie and Alan, were at the Harris Museum to remember Zena as "really cool, impulsive and creative".

"When you lose someone this wonderful, you lose every wonderful thing they would have done," said Alan.

For Sam, the exhibition has become much more than a collection of photographs.

Every image now has a name. Every face has a story.

Artists, teachers, writers, musicians, lawyers, and even an internationally famous DJ emerged from the photographs he took on Preston's streets.

Jon DaSilva went from Preston to DJing at the Hacienda and then on to producing and playing music around the world.

He believes there was a creativity in that generation, "a generation that often followed their dreams".

"I could have made more stacking shelves in Tesco but I loved music and I'm still in that world today," he said.

"It wasn't their status or the jobs they went on to have that made them special," he said.

Reflecting on his project, Sam believes the experience holds a wider message.

"Even if somebody is politically the extreme opposite of what you think, if you have a small connection with them, in this case it's a photo from 46 years ago, the conversation starts," he said.

"You suddenly realise the divide is something else.

"As human beings, we're basically all very similar."

After 46 years wondering what became of the young people he had photographed, Sam has had his answer.

In the process, he said he made 40 new friends.

The exhibition runs in Preston's Harris Museum until 10 January.

articles.title: Watch: Hundreds march in UK’s Gosport against migrant boat arrivals
articles.summary: Around 400 anti-migrant protesters in the United Kingdom marched through Hampshire’s Gosport on Sunday, against small boat arrivals in the town.
articles.body: Around 400 anti-migrant protesters in the United Kingdom marched through Hampshire’s Gosport on Sunday, against small boat arrivals in the town.An estimated 100 people took part in a separate counter-demonstration, organisers described as a Unity protest. BBC reported.Hampshire Police said both demonstrations passed without incident and no arrests were made. The force estimated that up to 550 people took part across the two protests.According to the BBC, Police imposed a ban on face coverings and issued a dispersal order covering part of the town until 20:00 GMT, allowing officers to tackle anti-social behaviour.The anti-migrant protesters marched from the Haslar Immigration Removal Centre (IRC), along Haslar Road and into the town square on a designated route. The Unity protest remained stationary at the far end of the high street, with police keeping the two groups apart.The demonstrations came amid opposition to plans to expand the Haslar facility, which is being redeveloped to accommodate up to 130 migrants who have no lawful right to remain in the UK before their deportation.The site has been closed since 2015, with redevelopment plans announced by the Conservative government in 2022. Earlier this year, the current government announced plans to add another 470 beds, beyond the original proposal for 130.Nearly 500 comments have been submitted on the planning application, with the majority opposing the expansion, BBC reported.Gosport has witnessed several anti-migrant protests in recent weeks following the arrival of small boat migrants near Haslar Marina and Fort Blockhouse.On September 6, hundreds of protesters gathered in Portsmouth, another city in Hampshire, after around 140 migrants arrived in a single dinghy that had crossed the English Channel. Two weeks later, migrants were intercepted south of the Isle of Wight.More than 100 protesters subsequently gathered in Gosport following reports that the migrants were being brought to the town. However, the lifeboats were ultimately diverted to Dover.At the beginning of October, a third boat carrying 150 migrants left Normandy for the Hampshire coast. articles.title: In 2022, Arsenal star Bukayo Saka funded 120 operations for children in Nigeria; four years later, his work with a charity that restored a Rwandan boy's sight has earned him the 2026 Socrates Award in London
articles.summary: Football’s biggest moments are often measured by goals, trophies and memorable nights under stadium lights.
articles.body: Football’s biggest moments are often measured by goals, trophies and memorable nights under stadium lights. But for Bukayo Saka, one of the most meaningful victories has come away from the pitch, in hospitals, classrooms and communities where access to basic medical care can transform a child’s future. The Arsenal star’s continued humanitarian efforts have now earned him one of football’s biggest off-pitch honors. Scroll down to find out the details of his humanitarian act.A recognition outside of footballSaka was named the winner of the 2026 Socrates Award at the Ballon d’Or ceremony in London, an award given to footballers whose humanitarian contributions extend beyond the sport, according to a report by The Cable. The prize, named in honor of the legendary Brazilian footballer, was first given in 2022 to former Liverpool forward Sadio Mane and has since become a major recognition of the role football plays in supporting social causes.The Standard reports Saka was recognized for his extensive humanitarian work with his family and several charitable organizations, particularly his long-standing involvement with Big Shoe, which provides medical assistance and humanitarian support to children and families in need around the world. The award was presented by Nigerian musician Burna Boy at the gala, held at the Palladium Theater in London, adds The Cable.Nigeria: 120 childrenSaka has worked with Big Shoe on initiatives to support children who may have trouble accessing necessary medical procedures, according to The Standard. In 2022, the Arsenal winger partnered with the charity to finance life-changing surgeries for 120 children in Kano, Nigeria, in one of the most significant efforts of his charitable work to date.His support went beyond Nigeria the following year. Saka also helped fund surgeries for another 100 children across Rwanda, Kenya and Tanzania, as part of broader efforts to bring critical healthcare to children in developing communities, The Cable reported. The work has a personal resonance with the cause. Saka, who is of Nigerian heritage, has long used his platform to support initiatives for children in situations vastly different from his own.Restoring a child’s visionAmong the stories featured around Saka’s Socrates Award was that of 14-year-old Biringiro from Rwanda, whose eyesight was restored thanks to Big Shoe’s medical program. Biringiro had started losing his sight at the age of 12, The Standard reports. Living in a village without electricity, his failing eyesight had made it increasingly difficult to move around each day and had impacted his ability to fully participate at school.Thanks to treatment supported by Big Shoe, the young boy was able to regain his sight and go back to activities that had become difficult, including reading the classroom blackboard. His story was a powerful testament to the impact behind Saka’s charitable work, turning the award from a personal achievement into recognition of the children and communities benefitting from the initiative.A wide-ranging missionSaka’s humanitarian efforts go beyond individual medical procedures. The footballer has been working with Big Shoe and his family to help children who do not have the same chances or resources as many others.The initiative also reflects the broader purpose of the Socrates Award: to highlight the ability of prominent athletes to use their visibility and influence to create meaningful change away from competition.Saka has emphasized the importance of helping children rediscover simple joys and possibilities that illness or poverty can take away, as The Standard reported. For young beneficiaries of Big Shoe’s work, that can mean something as fundamental as being able to see clearly, return to school or imagine a future without a medical condition that defines their possibilities.A different type of winThe 2026 Socrates Award adds another layer to Saka’s growing legacy. His footballing legacy with Arsenal may continue to define him, but his charitable work is creating an impact measured in lives, not in scorelines.Images Courtesy: Facebook and istockYou use AI every day. articles.title: Sir Tom Jones 'truly sorry' as he cancels concerts due to illness
articles.summary: Sir Tom has pushed back two concerts in the US on doctor's advice, due to "a bad case of the flu".
articles.body:
Sir Tom Jones said he is "truly sorry" after rescheduling two forthcoming concerts due to "a bad case of the flu".

The 86-year-old singer from Pontypridd, Rhondda Cynon Taf, is currently on his Come Gather Round world tour.

He announced the decision to push back his Monday show in Los Angeles, and Tuesday's concert in San Diego, following doctor's advice.

In a post on Instagram, he wrote: "Following doctor's advice, I unfortunately have to reschedule tonight's show in Los Angeles and tomorrow's show in San Diego."

The San Diego concert will now take place at The Rady Shell, at Jacobs Park, on 3 November, while his Los Angeles show has been moved to 4 November.

On Instagram, he wrote: "I've had a great time these last few weeks, completing 20 shows and singing for wonderful audiences across the USA, but unexpectedly I've been hit with a bad case of the flu."

He added: "I'm truly sorry for any inconvenience caused. I look forward to seeing you all soon.

"All tickets for the original dates will remain valid. However, if customers are unable to attend the rescheduled dates, they are advised to contact their original point of purchase for a refund."

The post was shared just hours before he was expected to perform at the Greek Theatre, with the Los Angeles venue among those wishing Sir Tom well.

The It's Not Unusual and What's New Pussycat? singer recently made headlines after revealing ITV had "made the decision" to "fire" him from The Voice UK coaching panel.

Sir Tom, who has served as an on-off coach on the popular singing competition since its 2012 debut, shared the news on Instagram last month, amid speculation he had been "dropped" from its 2027 series.

The Delilah and She's A Lady singer has achieved three UK number one singles and four chart-topping albums during a music career spanning more than six decades.

His awards include one Grammy, two Brits and an Ivor Novello; Sir Tom also received a knighthood from the late Queen Elizabeth II in 2006 for his services to music.

articles.title: Girl, 9, asks council to 'fight' in Torrington data centre row
articles.summary: About 100 people protest against plans for a data centre and battery energy storage site.
articles.body:
A nine-year-old girl has told councillors to "fight for our homes, community and landscape" in a row over plans for a giant data centre and battery energy storage site in the countryside.

Developer Xlinks wants to build the 1.5Gw AI data centre - which would be one of the biggest in Europe - near Torrington in north Devon in a Unesco biosphere.

The plans were first made public in June but local residents have used Freedom of Information requests to reveal the developer had been in discussions with Torridge District Council officials since March 2025.

The council said it was "standard practice for an organisation to consult with the local planning department" and no plans had yet been submitted.

Demelza, who lives nearby the proposed site, addressed Torridge District Council members on Monday at a full council meeting.

She said: "I'm very worried and anxious about the proposal because it's going to take away a huge area of land and change our home forever."

Demelza told councillors she wanted her future "to look green and beautiful", with "birds humming and singing and trees rustling".

She said: "It's your job to fight for local people, to fight for our homes, community and landscape."

The young girl asked council members to "do everything you can to protect our future and ensure this proposal does not go ahead".

She added: "The decision you will be making will affect me and all the other children in this area for the rest of our lives."

Xlinks has said the data campus would take up just over a third of an 850-acre (3.4 sq km) site between Great Torrington, Weare Gifford and Huntshaw, with the entire site being larger than Great Torrington.

About 100 people turned out to protest against the plans ahead of the Torridge District Council meeting.

The data centre proposals were not being discussed on Monday, but there were other public speakers who voiced their opposition, including Matt Whittaker, who played a recording of the noise of a data centre as he spoke.

Giles Atton, who also spoke in the meeting, said the boundary of the data centre would be 3m (10ft) away from his property.

He said: "It will cause irreparable damage to the lives of people in Torrington and the surrounding areas."

Atton said the development could also "set a very damaging precedent" for "Devon as a whole and the nation" if it was allowed to be built on "prime greenfield land".

Correspondence seen by the BBC which was released to campaigners after a Freedom of Information request shows Torridge District Council officers had a meeting with the developers in March 2025 to discuss the data centre plans.

The data centre would be made up of giant warehouses full of powerful computers used to run digital services.

Nobody from the district council provided any response to the public contributions on Monday but said written answers would be provided.

The council has said in a statement the pre-application process is "a confidential process between the applicant and the local planning authority".

It said: "During this time, it is standard practice for an organisation to consult with the local planning department to help inform the planning application and process."

It added that a pre-application response sent to the applicant was "not confirmation of any proposal but is intended to offer guidance".

Xlinks claims the data centre and battery energy storage centre would provide between 650 and 1,200 permanent jobs and generate £3.6bn annually for the local economy.

A spokesperson for Xlinks said in a statement said the firm was listening to "thoughts and concerns of North Devon residents which are helping to shape the plans for the Devon data campus".

The statement said plans were "at a relatively early stage" and would be shared with residents and councils "as soon as possible".

Xlinks had said it would hold public information days in July but those events were cancelled and no date has yet been set for when they might take place.

articles.title: Trump Accounts are just the beginning. Young Americans need a path to homeownership
articles.summary: A former FHA commissioner who enrolled daughter Margot in a Trump Account in March of 2025 proposes a Trump mortgage to slash homebuyer rates.
articles.body: In March of last year, my daughter Margot was born, and like any new father, I found myself thinking about the opportunities that would shape her future. I recently enrolled her in a Trump Account, President Donald Trump's initiative to help American children begin building wealth from an early age. With a $1,000 federal contribution for eligible children born between 2025 and 2028, the program gives the next generation an opportunity to benefit from decades of investment growth. As President Trump's former Federal Housing Administration commissioner, I also believe Trump Accounts should be just the beginning for how we can help young Americans build lasting wealth. In particular, I think we are at a pivotal point in American history to enact new policies to help generations of families achieve financial independence through owning their first home. At 20 years old, I purchased my first house for $200,000 using an FHA-insured mortgage that required just 3.5% down, or $7,000. I also benefited from an $8,000 first-time homebuyer tax credit. Today, that property has more than doubled in value. Yet I worry that the path to homeownership is becoming increasingly difficult for Margot’s generation. According to the National Association of Realtors, first-time buyers now account for just 21% of home purchases, the lowest share on record since tracking began in 1981. WHO WANTS THEIR CHILD TO BE A MILLIONAIRE? TRUMP HAS GIVEN YOU THAT CHANCE The natural next step after the president’s creation of Trump Accounts for young children is to help this same generation achieve the dream of homeownership. I believe this new policy should be called a Trump Mortgage program, which can be a national initiative designed to help qualified first-time homebuyers secure mortgage rates one to one-and-a-half percentage points below prevailing market rates. Here’s how we can develop the policy for the Trump Mortgage: First, the Treasury, Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac can immediately purchase the mortgage bonds backed by qualifying first-time homebuyer mortgages. The objective would be to facilitate the financing of these mortgages at lower rates using the secondary bond market, similar to a strategy already being deployed by Secretary Bessent and FHFA Director Pulte. TRUMP-BACKED HOUSING OVERHAUL TARGETING WALL STREET INVESTORS CLEARS SENATE The government should then hold onto these bonds while interest rates remain elevated and sell them when rates decline. It is important to note that this program won’t provide free money as Treasury, Fannie and Freddie are already in the business of buying mortgage-backed securities. Any program would have clear limits on its size, funding costs, prepayment risk and taxpayer exposure. Next, Congress should expand the use of existing tax-exempt mortgage financing. This isn’t some untested financial innovation. State housing finance agencies have been issuing tax-exempt mortgage revenue bonds for decades. Since investors generally accept lower yields when interest is exempt from federal income tax, eligible borrowers can benefit from lower mortgage rates. Congress already has bipartisan legislation proposed to expand the capacity of these programs. We should build on that existing model and explore whether a broader first-time homebuyer initiative like the Trump Mortgage program makes sense. Consider a young couple purchasing a $350,000 home with a $330,000 30-year mortgage. At a 6.5% interest rate, their monthly principal and interest payment would be approximately $2,086, but reducing that rate to 5% would lower the payment to roughly $1,772. For a family balancing childcare, groceries and the everyday expenses of raising children, saving more than $300 every month and $100,000 over the life of the loan that could be the difference between continuing to rent and finally purchasing a home. THE AMERICAN DREAM NOW COMES WITH A ZIP CODE: HERE'S WHERE STARTER HOMES ARE STILL WITHIN REACH Of course, lower mortgage rates alone will not solve America's housing shortage, and expanding access to financing must go hand in hand with policies that make it easier to build more homes. articles.title: A decade after liquor ban, Bihar faces a new drug question: What the numbers reveal
articles.summary: Punjab is set to go to polls in 2027, and the BJP, seeking to form its first government in the state, has made the drug menace a major election issue.
articles.body: Punjab is set to go to polls in 2027, and the BJP, seeking to form its first government in the state, has made the drug menace a major election issue. The party has been targeting the ruling Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) over its handling of the problem. Union home minister Amit Shah has even promised to make Punjab "drug-free" by December 2029 if the BJP comes to power.But AAP has hit back. Its national convener Arvind Kejriwal questioned the BJP over the drug problem in states where it is in power, including Bihar, Gujarat, Rajasthan and Goa, asking why the same deadline had not been set for them.The political exchange has also put the focus on Bihar, where alcohol has been banned for a decade but recent drug seizures have raised fresh concerns. More than 4.13 lakh intoxicating injections were seized in Patna in the first eight months of 2026, while investigations have uncovered heroin consignments, codeine-based cough syrup and networks involved in preparing and distributing narcotics.But what do these seizures actually reveal? Is Bihar witnessing a rise in drug consumption, or is the state increasingly becoming a transit route for narcotics headed elsewhere? And has a decade of prohibition had any bearing on the availability and use of other intoxicants? Here's what the data revealsDoes Bihar have a new drug problem?More than 4.13 lakh intoxicating injections seized in Patna in the first eight months of 2026. A sharp rise in smack seizures. Growing quantities of codeine-based cough syrup being intercepted. Across Bihar, recent drug seizures and investigations point to a changing narcotics landscape, raising questions about what is entering the state, where it is going and who is using it.But do these seizures signal a growing drug problem within Bihar, or are they exposing the scale of a trafficking network that uses the state as a transit route? Police have traced consignments from the Northeast and Nepal-linked routes, while investigations in Patna have uncovered alleged local networks involved in preparing and distributing narcotics.The answers are not straightforward. Five years of seizure data show sharp fluctuations rather than a consistent rise across substances. Meanwhile, a debate over Bihar’s liquor prohibition has raised another question about whether the use of alternative intoxicants has changed since the ban came into force in 2016.(function(){function e(){window.addEventListener(`message`,function(e){if(e.data[`datawrapper-height`]!==void 0){var t=document.querySelectorAll(`iframe`);for(var n in e.data[`datawrapper-height`])for(var r=0,i;i=t[r];r++)if(i.contentWindow===e.source){var a=e.data[`datawrapper-height`][n]+`px`;i.style.height=a}}})}e()})();What do the numbers reveal?Bihar’s drug seizure data over five years shows that ganja accounted for the largest quantities seized among the major narcotics listed, while seizures of heroin fluctuated sharply. Ganja seizures rose from 16,607 kg in 2020 to 33,603 kg in 2021, before falling to 23,023 kg in 2022 and 13,129 kg in 2023. They increased again to 18,356 kg in 2024.Heroin seizures fell from 363.77 kg in 2020 to 9.62 kg in 2021, before rising to 31.13 kg in 2022, 27.37 kg in 2023 and 53.35 kg in 2024. Hashish seizures also varied, peaking at 395.12 kg in 2021 before declining to 195 kg in 2024.A person whose circle consumes drugs said, on the condition of anonymity, that marijuana remained the most widely consumed substance in their social circle and that they had not noticed a significant shift in preferences towards other drugs.“In most circles, marijuana is most widely consumed, and I don't think synthetic drugs have made their way to Bihar,” the person said.The data records smaller seizures of other substances, including ATS, cocaine and LSD in certain years. While these figures show fluctuations in the quantities of narcotics seized, they do not establish a steady year-on-year rise in drug trafficking or consumption. Seizure figures reflect what enforcement agencies intercept and, on their own, cannot establish how many people use drugs or whether drug abuse is increasing in Bihar.Where are the drugs coming from?Police say a significant share of narcotics reaching Patna comes from the Northeast. The routes and methods of transportation vary according to the size of a consignment.Investigations have also pointed to supply chains passing through multiple states. In September, four people were arrested near JP Setu in Patna with 274 gm of heroin. Police traced the consignment to Assam, from where it allegedly travelled to Tamkuhi in Kushinagar, Uttar Pradesh, before being sent towards Patna.Bihar’s location along the Nepal border adds another dimension to the problem. On October 25, Motihari Police, in a joint operation with the Bihar Special Task Force, seized smack valued at Rs 4 crore near Raxaul, close to the India-Nepal border.In a separate operation, the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence’s Muzaffarpur unit and the Bihar STF busted a suspected network involved in smuggling Nepal-origin charas into India. Two people were arrested and 5.14 kg of charas, valued by officials at Rs 5.14 crore, was seized. Investigators said the consignment was intended for onward transportation to Indore in Madhya Pradesh.The cases point to Bihar’s role as a route for narcotics moving between regions. However, seizures along transport corridors do not establish how much of the intercepted supply is consumed within the state.Is the trade limited to transportation?Police investigations suggest that local networks are also involved in storage, preparation and distribution.In March, police found a rented room in Patna’s Ramakrishna Nagar area allegedly being used to prepare smack. A flat in Alamganj was allegedly used for distribution. Police recovered 1.68 kg of brown sugar and cash, along with cheques worth around Rs 70 lakh issued in the name of a police officer.The trade is not confined to substances traditionally associated with narcotics smuggling. Pharmaceutical products have also featured in investigations. In May, the DRI seized 7,500 bottles of codeine-based cough syrup from a pickup van outside Patna’s Rajendra Nagar Terminal. Investigators found that the consignee’s drug licence had been cancelled and that the firm did not exist at its stated address.Such cases raise questions about how pharmaceutical products enter illicit supply chains, how they are distributed and whether existing monitoring systems are able to detect diversion from legitimate channels.A Patna high court order has raised questions about how narcotics can travel long distances before being intercepted.In an order dated September 15, the court expressed concern over two minor boys who had travelled from Assam to Bihar in a car without a registration certificate. The vehicle was intercepted near Patna, and the directorate of revenue intelligence recovered more than 60 kg of cannabis from a concealed compartment.The court questioned how the vehicle had travelled uninterrupted from Assam to Bihar while carrying a commercial quantity of cannabis.(function(){function e(){window.addEventListener(`message`,function(e){if(e.data[`datawrapper-height`]!==void 0){var t=document.querySelectorAll(`iframe`);for(var n in e.data[`datawrapper-height`])for(var r=0,i;i=t[r];r++)if(i.contentWindow===e.source){var a=e.data[`datawrapper-height`][n]+`px`;i.style.height=a}}})}e()})();Has prohibition changed pattern of substance use?Bihar banned the sale and consumption of alcohol in April 2016 under a policy introduced by the Nitish Kumar government. The prohibition was intended, among other objectives, to reduce domestic violence and encourage households to spend money on more productive needs.A research paper by the National Council of Applied Economic Research (NCAER), titled Macro Perspective of Bihar's Development Achievements, Unfinished Agenda, and the Way Forward, has questioned whether the ban achieved its intended outcomes.The paper said reported crimes against women had not declined following prohibition and that total reported crimes against women increased over the post-2016 period. It also pointed to concerns about the expansion of illicit liquor trade, enforcement challenges, corruption and the use of alternative intoxicants, including illicit drugs."In tandem, there was a significant rise in illegal liquor trade leading to higher alcohol consumption, increased crime and corruption, and an increase in the use of alternative additive substances, such as illicit drugs," the paper said.The authors argued that Bihar should reconsider prohibition and restore alcohol excise duty to historical levels. They estimated that doing so could increase the state’s own revenues by 14-15%.Some residents also believe prohibition may be one factor behind the availability of other intoxicants, although personal accounts cannot establish a direct link between the ban and drug consumption.“I would argue that it is a byproduct of the prohibition in the state, but that isn't the full picture,” another person who spoke on condition of anonymity said, referring to the perceived increase in drug availability.The person said their observations were based on the experiences of people in their social circle who use drugs, adding that young people and those in their 30s appeared to be among the users they had noticed.“In a state like Bihar, with a large chunk of youth population that haven't so far been backed with job opportunities, [this] has also contributed to the rise of drug consumption in the state,” the person said.They also flagged a lack of awareness about addiction and the support available to people who use drugs.“I feel like there is a lack of awareness against remedial methods, like what to do if someone you know has become addicted to drugs, what are you supposed to do then. I feel like there is a lack of rehabilitation system and awareness among the people needed to curb the drug menace,” the person said.Is Bihar seeing a rise in consumption or a rise in detection?The distinction matters because seizures measure what enforcement agencies intercept, not the total volume of drugs entering the market or being consumed.Bihar’s prohibition and narcotics enforcement policies also form part of a wider debate over how the state measures the effectiveness of its policing. A rise in seizures can reflect an increase in trafficking, improved detection or a combination of both.(function(){function e(){window.addEventListener(`message`,function(e){if(e.data[`datawrapper-height`]!==void 0){var t=document.querySelectorAll(`iframe`);for(var n in e.data[`datawrapper-height`])for(var r=0,i;i=t[r];r++)if(i.contentWindow===e.source){var a=e.data[`datawrapper-height`][n]+`px`;i.style.height=a}}})}e()})();Bihar minister Madan Sahni has rejected the charge that rising seizures indicate a failure of prohibition. He said the increase was not confined to Bihar but was a phenomenon seen in other states as well."I must say that due to the alertness of the officials concerned, the quantity of the seizure of substances prohibited under the NDPS Act has increased in the state, but at the same time, people should know that the majority of the prohibited substances seized in Bihar are meant for supply to other states," he said.Sahni added that intercepting consignments within Bihar could create the impression that the drugs were intended for local consumption, even when they were being transported elsewhere. He also defended prohibition, saying it had been successful.The minister’s argument points to an important gap in the available figures. Without comparable data on drug use, treatment demand, drug-related health emergencies and the destinations of intercepted consignments, it is difficult to determine how much of the rise reflects local consumption.RJD MP Manoj Kumar Jha, meanwhile, cited a media report and said the situation was out of control."An entire generation has been ruined. This is what happens when the government has no control. The situation here is completely out of control..." he said.Does Bihar have a new drug problem?Bihar’s recent seizure figures and investigations point to a changing narcotics landscape. Police have reported sharp increases in some categories, identified supply routes running through several states and uncovered alleged local networks involved in preparation and distribution. Seizures near the Nepal border have also highlighted the state’s role in cross-border trafficking.But the central question remains unresolved. Is Bihar facing a growing drug-consumption problem, a trafficking problem that extends beyond its borders, or both?Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Man waited 3 months for a silver Royal Enfield Classic 350 but got a blue one; consumer commission found dealer guilty and ordered it to pay Rs 28,000, with interest
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: A district consumer commission in Kerala has held a Royal Enfield dealer guilty of unfair trade practice after a customer who booked a silver
articles.body: NEW DELHI: A district consumer commission in Kerala has held a Royal Enfield dealer guilty of unfair trade practice after a customer who booked a silver Classic 350 motorcycle was made to take a lagoon blue model following a delay of around three months.The commission, in its October 23 order, also found that the dealer had provided incorrect manufacturing details in the vehicle’s registration certificate. It directed the dealer to pay Rs 25,000 as compensation and Rs 3,000 towards litigation costs, with interest on the compensation if payment was delayed.Silver Classic 350 disputeAccording to the commission’s order, the complainant, Krishnakumar S Nair, booked a silver Royal Enfield Classic 350 from Sivaji Motors on September 3, 2016, with a waiting period of 60 days.The complainant alleged that the dealer initially told him the motorcycle would be delivered in the first week of November, but he was later told that delivery would only be possible by November 28. He was asked to make the payment in the meantime so that the paperwork could be completed.However, when he visited the showroom, he was told that the dealer did not have a silver motorcycle in stock and that delivery could take until January 2017.According to the complaint, Nair accepted the lagoon blue colour because he was a defence personnel member who had to leave for his native place to join duty. He paid Rs 99,550 on December 7 and another Rs 40,000 on December 8, 2016.However, when he went to collect the motorcycle on December 12, he alleged that the vehicle was covered in dust and mud and that its front disc brake and handle lock had problems. He was allegedly told that the issues would be addressed during the first servicing.The complainant further alleged that he saw a new silver Classic 350 being delivered to another customer at the showroom, despite having been told that the dealer had no silver bike available. He also claimed that the vehicle’s manufacturing year was incorrectly recorded in the registration documents, which created problems during inspection by the Motor Vehicles Department.According to the complaint, the registration certificate was eventually issued on January 3, 2017.Sivaji Motors denied the allegations. It claimed that the customer had been informed that silver bikes were unavailable and had agreed to take the lagoon blue model. The dealer also denied that the motorcycle was dirty or faulty and sought dismissal of the complaint.The manufacturer, Royal Enfield, did not appear before the commission and was proceeded against ex parte.Commission’s findingThe bench comprising president P V Jayarajan and members Preetha G Nair and Viju V R, examined the booking form, payment receipts, registration certificates and communications produced by the complainant.It noted that the booking form recorded a waiting period of 60 days and that the customer had booked a silver motorcycle. The dealer had not produced stock records or other documents showing the availability of silver and lagoon blue motorcycles at the relevant time.The commission observed that the dealer could have produced its stock register and its records of vehicles received from the manufacturer and sold to customers to support its defence.“Hence, here in this case the opposite party has failed to produce the best evidence available with them and an adverse inference has to be drawn against the opposite parties,” the bench noted.The commission also noted the discrepancy in the manufacturing details recorded in the registration certificate. It found that the customer had been put to further trouble after waiting for around three months and not receiving the colour of motorcycle he had originally booked.“From the available evidence before this Commission, we find that there is deficiency in service and unfair trade practice on the part of the 1st opposite party,” it added.However, the commission rejected the request to replace the motorcycle with a new one. It said that a consumer seeking replacement on the ground of a manufacturing defect must establish the defect, including through expert evidence. No such evidence had been produced in this case.The commission also held that the manufacturer could not be made liable merely for the dealer’s actions when no specific allegation or proof established deficiency in service or unfair trade practice on the manufacturer’s part.Final orderPartly allowing the complaint, the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, Thiruvananthapuram, directed Sivaji Motors to:Pay Rs 25,000 as compensation.Pay Rs 3,000 towards litigation costs.The total amount ordered was Rs 28,000. The dealer was directed to comply within 30 days of receiving the order. If it failed to do so, the compensation amount, excluding litigation costs, would carry interest at 9 percent per annum from the date of the order until payment.The commission did not order replacement of the motorcycle or a refund of its purchase price.

articles.title: Carville advises Dems cater to one key demographic for 2028 nominee, but warns 'they're not that liberal'
articles.summary: James Carville says southern Black voters should guide the 2028 Democratic nominee, warning the party not to hand power to "overly educated people."
articles.body: Veteran Democratic strategist James Carville advised Democrats on Sunday that they need to pay attention to what Black southerners want when picking a nominee for 2028, warning they are not a very socially liberal demographic. Political strategist Mark McKinnon spoke to Carville on the most recent episode of the "Politics War Room" podcast, noting the 2028 Democratic presidential primary will begin in South Carolina. When he asked Carville what impact that might have, the Democratic strategist offered one key piece of advice for the party. "The key, single most important voting demographic in selecting a Democratic nominee is, was, and should continue to be southern Blacks," Carville said. "There's no more loyal constituency in the party. And by the way, just so people understand this, they're not that liberal, OK?" "And what they want and what we're going to find out, and there's an expression, is, ‘I don't want someone that's talk the talk. I want somebody that's walk the walk.’ And when you go to South Carolina and make a pitch — advice from James Carville — talk about things you've done," Carville continued. WARNOCK WARNS DEMS TO CUT THE 'JARGON' AND SPEAK 'PLAIN ENGLISH' WITH YOUNG MEN WHO FEEL LEFT BEHIND He then parodied recent Democratic Party rhetoric, saying, "Don't say, ‘I am a great friend of people of color.’ That's the stupidest f---ing expression I ever heard." He advised that if a politician can actually show they have provided opportunities for Black Americans, then they will have actual credibility. Meanwhile, ideologically far-left intellectuals, he warned, would steer the party in an unwise direction, warning, "But don't ever take power of nomination away from southern Blacks. 'Cause if you give it to overly educated people, overly educated people f--- everything up." "As long as that's there," he said of Black southerners being the core guidance of the Democrats’ 2028 nominee pick, "we're going to have a pretty good nomination." BLACK VOTERS, JEWISH DEMOCRATS IN MICHIGAN WARY OF VOTING FOR EL-SAYED, SAY 'HE'S TAKING ADVANTAGE' Democrat Dan Turrentine, co-host of "The Huddle," concurred in a statement to Fox News Digital about Carville’s comments. "James is right. The average Black voter, like most Americans, is not crazy liberal," he said. "They are most interested in what you will do to solve today’s problems versus wasting time fantasizing about tomorrow’s revolution. That said, it’s likely the winning candidate will not view this as an ‘either/or’ choice, but find a way to appeal to ‘both’ constituencies." articles.title: 'I don't believe in Russia's humanity': Truce brings hope to starving Ukraine city of Oleshky
articles.summary: A ceasefire has taken effect in the Russian-occupied Ukrainian city of Oleshky, offering a potential lifeline to residents trapped without food, water and
articles.body: A ceasefire has taken effect in the Russian-occupied Ukrainian city of Oleshky, offering a potential lifeline to residents trapped without food, water and electricity for years, as a humanitarian operation is planned to deliver supplies and evacuate civilians.Ukraine's human rights commissioner Dmytro Lubinets confirmed that Kyiv was honouring the truce, while Russia's defence ministry said it had halted fire towards the Ukrainian-controlled city of Kherson across the Dnipro River.The White House has credited US First Lady Melania Trump with securing the ceasefire, which is intended to facilitate aid deliveries and civilian evacuations.Oleshky lies in Ukraine's southern Kherson region, on the eastern bank of the Dnipro River, which separates it from Ukrainian-controlled territory.Russian forces seized the town during the opening days of Moscow's full-scale invasion in February 2022. The town had a pre-war population of around 24,000, but Ukraine estimates that about 6,000 people, including 200 children, remain in Oleshky and its surrounding areas.The humanitarian situation has deteriorated sharply, with shops closed and residents deprived of electricity, gas and running water for three years. Attempts to deliver supplies have repeatedly failed, while mined roads and the threat of renewed fighting have made it dangerous for civilians to leave.With food running out, some residents have resorted to cooking weeds gathered from their gardens to survive. Others face shortages of medicine and inadequate access to medical care, leaving vulnerable residents particularly exposed as winter approaches."I don't believe in Russia's humanity," one resident told the BBC, expressing doubts about whether the ceasefire would hold long enough for civilians to escape safely.The planned evacuation also carries risks. Roads remain mined, communications are patchy and residents fear renewed shooting, reprisals or detention if their phones and online activity reveal support for Ukraine.One woman told the BBC she was recovering in hospital after undergoing two surgeries following a landmine explosion and was worried she would be unable to join the evacuation.The White House said civilian representatives from Russia and Ukraine would work together to visit residents and assess their needs.You use AI every day.
