articles.title: The Netherlands pulls out of Eurovision 2027 due to Israel ‘sensitivities’
articles.summary: Dutch withdrawal is the latest in a number of boycotts by countries unhappy about Israel’s inclusion.
articles.body:
The Netherlands has withdrawn from next year’s Eurovision Song Contest, its public broadcaster NPO has confirmed, citing “sensitivities” over Israel’s participation.

“We have known for some time that Israel’s participation elicits various reactions in society and causes discussion and division,” the NPO’s media director Jurre Bosman said in a statement.

“Therefore, after consultation with the board of broadcasters, the NPO has decided to forgo participation in 2027.”

The announcement follows a decision in August by Dutch broadcaster AVROTROS to boycott the competition. AVROTROS, which usually selects the Netherlands’ entry and broadcasts the show, said the event could “no longer be considered neutral”.

NPO stepped in last month, saying it would take responsibility for the Dutch entry to the competition, before reversing course on Tuesday.

Jet de Ranitz, NPO’s executive chairman, acknowledged that the decision would disappoint fans but stressed that the contest would still be aired on public channels.

“Due to the sensitivities surrounding the themes currently at play, we have decided to take a step back for the time being,” De Ranitz said.

The announcement follows the Netherlands’ boycott of the 2026 edition. Iceland, Spain, Ireland, and Slovenia all pulled out, with the latter three refusing to broadcast the show at all.

In August, the organisers announced that countries would be unable to host the competition if “an armed conflict, a sensitive geopolitical situation, or any other situation materially affects the security, safety or stability of their state or immediate region.”

But that has not prevented withdrawals, with Ireland already having announced that it will not be participating in next year’s contest for the second year in a row.

Earlier this month, the Czech broadcaster also pulled out of next year’s event, but cited spending cuts as the reason.

Bulgaria will host next year’s edition of Eurovision for the first time in the Black Sea city of Burgas, after Bulgarian singer Darina Yotova, known as Dara, won this year’s contest in Vienna, Austria, with her catchy floor-filler ‘Bangaranga’.

Since its first edition in 1956, Eurovision has become the world’s biggest live televised music event. It catapulted Swedish icons ABBA to worldwide fame, as well as boosting artists such as Celine Dion and Olivia Newton-John.

articles.title: How two Staffordshire landscapers caught Erling Haaland's eye
articles.summary: A prank challenge sparked millions of views online and a surprise response from the footballer.
articles.body:
A go-karting trip is on the cards for staff at a landscaping business after footballer Erling Haaland responded to their online plea.

Staffordshire landscaper Shane Hassall made a video asking colleague Wade Taylor for a day off to go karting. He was told he could, if his video was viewed more than 100,000 times and got a comment from the Norwegian international player.

To their surprise their social media video got more than 16 million views in a couple of days but the pair had to wait to see if the Manchester City striker would respond.

Last week, a response came from Haaland, who commented on Thursday evening. His first message simply said: "Enjoy", with a second following shortly afterwards: "Your evening just became a bit better."

"We're just humble landscapers and we just decided to have a laugh," Taylor told BBC Radio Stoke.

The video was posted on Tuesday and, after attracting hundreds of thousands of likes, got the attention of Haaland two days later.

Taylor said he had a feeling the challenge would somehow work.

"To be honest with you, I don't know. I had no doubt that it was going to happen," he told BBC Radio Stoke.

"Once he'd made that commitment and we'd posted it, I just had this weird feeling that it was going to happen. We got 100,000 likes within the first four hours, which was crazy.

"People were commenting saying, 'We need this'. The community was building pretty quickly and the phone was buzzing."

Hassall said: "Because we're always pranking each other, I thought he was winding me up," he laughed.

The viral success led to TeamSport in Burslem offering the team a free go-karting session, allowing them to complete the challenge.

Despite the millions of views, Taylor said little had changed about their day-to-day lives.

He said: "We've arrived here today in a van. It's no joke that we're just working day in and day out. After this interview we're going to go and install a fence."

The company, Maple Landscapes, works across Staffordshire and Cheshire, and last year made a conscious decision to focus more heavily on social media as a marketing tool.

Since then, a series of prank-style videos have helped build a growing audience online.

Now, after their unexpected viral success, Taylor and Hassall are already plotting their next challenge.

The pair told the BBC they hope to raise money for BBC Children in Need by securing 500,000 likes on a future video and a comment from England captain, Harry Kane.

If they succeed, they have pledged to walk from Stoke-on-Trent to Salford Quays.

"We want to give something back," they said.

"What an opportunity to be on here and if we can do something for someone else, I think that'll be amazing."

articles.title: Russia targets Kyiv as Finnish, Norwegian leaders hold rare call with Putin
articles.summary: Strikes hit a major bridge in the Ukrainian capital as leaders push for ‘direct discussions’ to end the war.
articles.body:
Russia has attacked transport infrastructure in Ukraine’s capital, targeting a major bridge, as the leaders of Finland and Norway held a rare call with Russian President Vladimir Putin and a separate one with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy.

Officials in Kyiv said the South Bridge was hit in overnight attacks on the city ⁠⁠that included 16 ballistic missiles and more ⁠⁠than 280 drones. Zelenskyy said Russian forces struck again while emergency crews were still dealing with the aftermath of the initial strikes.

“This is a serious escalation in Russia’s campaign targeting our logistics,” he said.

Russian attacks also caused deaths and injuries in the cities of Kharkiv and Pavlohrad.

Russia’s Defence Ministry said on Telegram that its forces had targeted transport infrastructure in Kyiv and a logistics hub in the Kharkiv region, along with industrial sites and cargo vessels it said were serving military purposes.

Officials in the Russian-controlled part of Ukraine’s southeastern Zaporizhzhia region said a drone strike on a bus killed one person and injured 30 others.

One person was also killed and six others were wounded in a drone attack on the Russian city of Bryansk, near the Ukrainian border.

The attacks come as the warring sides prepare for talks. On Friday, Kyiv and Moscow said they had agreed to hold United States-mediated technical meetings in Abu Dhabi in early November.

Finnish President Alexander Stubb and Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Store called Putin from Helsinki on Tuesday to convey messages on future negotiations ahead of the Abu Dhabi meetings, according to a statement from both governments.

Zelenskyy, who spoke to the pair afterwards, said on X that they had told Putin real steps were needed to de-escalate attacks on Ukraine’s energy facilities and infrastructure. He said they also discussed preparations for the November talks.

“There must be peace, de-escalation is needed, and Russia must stop dragging out the war,” he said.

In the Finnish-Norwegian statement, Stubb said the war’s outcome would directly affect the security of Finland and Norway, both of which border Russia, and of Europe more widely.

“Ending the war requires direct discussions,” he said.

Store said the two leaders had stressed the importance of de-escalation during the call.

Both leaders said they spoke for their own countries, not Europe, and that Finnish and Norwegian support for Ukraine would continue.

Most Western European leaders have avoided direct contact with Putin since Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine began in February 2022.

The calls come amid a renewed US push to end the war. The two governments described Tuesday’s call, held in consultation with Ukraine, as a follow-up to talks in Oslo on October 20 with Zelenskyy and US special envoy Steve Witkoff.

Witkoff met Putin in St Petersburg the next day, after which the Kremlin said it was ready to resume US-mediated talks with Kyiv that stalled in February.

US President Donald Trump has also credited his wife, First Lady Melania Trump, with securing a localised ceasefire in the southern Kherson region, which took effect on Tuesday to allow aid into the Russian-controlled town of Oleshky.

articles.title: Nature: New strategy to restore protection for nature in Northern Ireland launched
articles.summary: About 40% of the plants and animals in protected sites across Northern Ireland fall short of meeting the standard for "favourable condition".
articles.body:
A new strategy to restore and enhance protection for nature in Northern Ireland has been launched by the agriculture and environment minister.

About 40% of the plants and animals in protected sites across Northern Ireland fall short of meeting the standard for "favourable condition".

And just one of 49 priority habitat types - like ancient and native woodlands, blanket bogs and species-rich grasslands - have favourable status.

The Nature Recovery Strategy sets out a long-term framework based on science for tackling biodiversity loss and restoring habitats.

Minister Andrew Muir said supporting nature was "not just a nice thing to do", but "a moral obligation to future generations".

But the minister acknowledged that money would be needed to address the challenges.

The strategy highlights the importance of nature as providing the food we eat, the water we drink and the air we breathe.

Muir said nature must be put "back at the heart of everything we do, because when nature thrives, people flourish.

"It is essential to a strong economy, healthier communities and a more resilient Northern Ireland.

"With so much of our natural world lost, we must protect what remains, restore what has been damaged and create new habitats at scale."

Many places in Northern Ireland support rare or threatened plants, animals and habitats.

They can be legally designated to help ensure better management and protection of those species.

There are hundreds of such designated sites across Northern Ireland, covering around 10% of the land and 38% of coastal waters - classed as Areas of Special Scientific Interest; Special Areas of Conservation (SACs) which have international biodiversity importance; Ramsar Sites which cover wetlands of international importance; Special Protection Areas (SPAs); and Marine Conservation Zones (MCZs).

That should lead to work to protect the species and habitats they have been designated for.

The number of sites that were in favourable condition dropped from 61.7% in 2008, to 51.5% in 2024.

It is now investigating how those sites are being managed by the Department of Agriculture, Environment and Rural Affairs, after it found implementation of the designation fell short.

Northern Ireland is one of the most nature-depleted areas in the world, according to the 2023 State of Nature Report.

It found 12% of species here are under threat of extinction, and the number of flowering plants had declined by 14% since 1970.

The Nature Recovery Strategy identifies six external pressures affecting nature and biodiversity - invasive species; climate change; human impact through inappropriate development; land and sea-use change; increased intensive farming; pollution.

It says these must all be addressed effectively to allow nature to thrive.

articles.summary: Kerala CM V D Satheesan says govt will strengthen mechanisms for timely action on assembly committee reports, addressing delays and improving coordination.
articles.body: Thiruvananthapuram: Chief minister V D Satheesan on Tuesday said govt would take strong measures to ensure timely action on recommendations made by legislative assembly committees, acknowledging that delays in implementing their reports and obtaining information required by them were serious concerns.Replying to a submission in the assembly by V T Balram, Satheesan said govt would consider establishing a more effective mechanism to deal with committee reports, in consultation with the speaker. articles.title: 'Cannot call anybody by that name': HC directs ex-finance secretary to mute podcast remarks against BJP MP Nishikant Dubey
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The Delhi high court on Tuesday directed former finance secretary Subhash Chandra Garg to block or mute certain allegedly objectionable remarks
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Delhi high court on Tuesday directed former finance secretary Subhash Chandra Garg to block or mute certain allegedly objectionable remarks he made about BJP MP Nishikant Dubey on a podcast.Justice Tushar Rao Gedela noted that both Dubey and Garg were “persons of repute” and stressed that the former finance secretary should not have used an “intemperate word” during a YouTube podcast.“You cannot use a word like this. Suppose someone said ...(that to you), will you take that lightly? You cannot use the word. It is absolutely derogatory. You cannot call anybody by that name. Rest of the things, it is a debatable issue,” Justice Gedela orally observed during the hearing.Following instructions from Garg, his counsel assured the court that the retired bureaucrat would contact the podcast host to have the alleged defamatory phrases muted.However, Garg’s counsel argued that an interim injunction was unwarranted in the absence of any “aggravating circumstances”, particularly as more than a month had passed since the podcast’s release. Dubey had sought the injunction, alleging that Garg made false and malicious remarks against him during a podcast on September 17, which was subsequently published and circulated on YouTube, Facebook and other digital platforms.Before moving the Delhi high court, Dubey had issued a legal notice to Garg on September 21, demanding the immediate withdrawal and retraction of the alleged defamatory remarks, along with their removal from digital platforms.Trinamool Congress MP Mahua Moitra’s counsel also assured the court that she would remove certain related posts on X that were alleged to be defamatory.However, the lawyer maintained that Moitra would retain her right to speak on the broader issue raised in her posts.The judge issued summons to Garg and Moitra in connection with Dubey’s defamation suit, which seeks permanent and mandatory injunctions restraining them from making further allegedly defamatory remarks against him, an apology and damages of Rs 2 crore.The court also directed them to file their replies.(With PTI inputs)Get the latest India News and Live updates.
